learning_outcomes.text: Knows the fundamental notions of professional ethics, the differences between ethics, morality, deontology, integrity.
Understands the principles and legal standards regarding good conduct in research, development, innovation activities (Law 206/2004).
Has knowledge about plagiarism prevention and combat, about the ethics of scientific writing and academic responsibility.
Understands the relevant provisions of the Labor Code and the University and Industry Professional Ethics and Deontology Codes.
Knows the essential concepts regarding corruption, transparency, conflict of interest, and integrity whistleblowers.
Uses digital tools for presenting specialized works.
Plans the stages of drafting a report on a subject related to the course topic.
Operates with concepts specific to this discipline.

Respects ethical principles, norms, and values in the correct and timely execution of professional tasks, by adopting a rigorous, efficient, and responsible work strategy in decision-making for problem-solving.
Integrates into the workgroup and applies effective relational and teamwork techniques in multidisciplinary teams, at various hierarchical levels.
Continuously informs and documents themselves in their field of activity by adequately using effective lifelong learning methods and techniques.

syllabus_topics: General notions of ethics and integrity. Objectives, methods, definitions, interdisciplinary approaches. Connection with morality

Traditions in ethics and integrity, theoretical ethics related to applied ethics, vulnerabilities, consequences, probabilities of manifestation and risks in activity. Consequences of violating ethical principles
About plagiarism. Definitions, history, famous examples, similarity
Provisions of Law no. 206/2004 regarding good conduct in scientific research
Harassment and inappropriate behavior in the collective
Methodology for developing codes of ethics and integrity
Provisions of the code of ethics and professional deontology of UT Iasi
Conceiving, structuring, and drafting a bachelor's thesis. Ethics and plagiarism issues
Legislation in the field of ethics
Analysis of the Ethics Committee report
teaching_methods: debates based on Power Point presentations
learning by discovery models facilitated by direct or indirect exploration of reality

assessment_methods.method: Individual/Team assignments and case study report (part of Examen/Colocviu)
Formative evaluation test (mid-term checks, part of Examen/Colocviu)
Summative evaluation test (final check, part of Examen/Colocviu)

assessment_rules: The student passes the Ethics and Integrity course if they demonstrate knowledge and understanding of the fundamental principles of professional and academic ethics, the ability to identify and apply moral conduct norms and integrity in university and professional activities, and adopt a responsible, honest, and respectful behavior towards the values of the institution and society. The final evaluation result is derived by considering the scores and weights allocated to each activity within the course. Grades will be awarded from 1 to 10, with a grade of 5 certifying the achievement of the minimum learning outcomes for a discipline and the granting of its associated study credits.
